items.title: Subsidies the fuel as household battery demand 'straps on a rocket'
items.description: Even as Australia appears to have passed the peak of solar uptake, demand for batteries is seemingly headed into orbit.

items.title: Mother says sending son to swim 4km for help 'one of the hardest decisions'
items.description: A WA mother says asking her teenage son to swim four kilometres through rough seas to get help after their family was swept out to sea, was "one of the hardest decisions" she has ever made.

items.title: The government has options to fight inflation, but most are unpopular
items.description: The federal government has a variety of options available if it wants to do more to stave off inflation, but none are popular.

items.title: 'Sorry for our children': Rate hike highlights plight of borrowers vs boomers
items.description: A third of Australians could benefit if banks raise deposit rates on savings, while mortgage holders are having to decide what to cut back on.

items.title: US forces shoot down Iranian drone near American warship

items.title: One Nation, a popular premier and independents: SA Liberals face three major threats
items.description: While South Australia is considered a more moderate state than Queensland or New South Wales, March's state election will still be a chance to gauge the seriousness of One Nation's polling surge and the impact of the Coalition split on the Liberal Party's brand.

items.title: French police raid X offices in Paris as Musk summoned to hearing

items.title: Signs of forced entry at Arizona home of Today show host Savannah Guthrie's mother
items.description: Investigators have also reportedly found evidence of a deliberate night time kidnapping at the property.

items.title: Mandelson set to retire from British politics over links to Epstein
items.description: The former UK ambassador to the US is set to retire from Britain's parliament on Wednesday as a possible criminal investigation looms over his ties to the late paedophile.

items.title: AI bots have created a religion, but experts say that's not the scary part
items.description: A social network run entirely by AI bots has attracted more than a million users — but experts warn it is not what the bots are saying that poses the true risk.

items.title: Missing bushwalker found alive in the Blue Mountains

items.title: The 'red line' that distinguishes PTSD from other conditions

items.title: Back to school tough for parents dealing with 'school can't'
items.description: Thousands of Australian parents are struggling with children who cannot go to school. A new podcast and e-book have been released to help support them.

items.title: Son of Norway's crown princess denies rape but admits lesser charges in court
items.description: Marius Borg Hoiby pleaded not guilty to four counts of rape and one of domestic violence.

items.title: 'Dispersed' Milan Cortina Games a learning opportunity for Brisbane 2032

items.title: Female athletes work smarter, to thrive in sport and professional careers

items.title: Disability expert slams 'dangerous narrative' of Mosman Park teen deaths

items.title: LIV golfers to start earning ranking points for top 10 finishes

items.title: Sprinklers are mandatory in aged care, but missing from specialist disability homes

items.title: Researchers hope 'spas' and 'saunas' could save the world's frogs

items.title: Thousands of foreigners look for way home after 'mass exodus' from scam compounds

items.title: ‘It could have caused many deaths’: Bomb attack condemned
